name: Spot response to a perpetual liquidation cascade
description: Event-shaped reading of how the composite spot reference moved after a perpetual liquidation cascade. A cascade begins at the first decision instant at which any configured derivatives venue's published btc.<v>.liquidation_pressure@1.0.0 clustering_state transitions into cascade; that instant is burst_time, burst_sequence increments by one, reference_price_at_burst is the ready reference_price of btc.external.spot_reference@1.0.0 at that instant, burst_notional_usd is the sum of the fresh configured venues' published notional_usd_60s, and burst_side follows the upstream normalized side skew: btc.<v>.liquidation_pressure@1.0.0 publishes side_skew_60s as (long_notional_usd_60s minus short_notional_usd_60s) divided by their total over the 60 second window, where a buy-side liquidation is counted as a long position being liquidated (Bybit allLiquidation S=Buy, ruling E55), so a summed side_skew_60s above zero is longs_liquidated, below zero is shorts_liquidated, and exactly zero is balanced; the summed value stays within [-1, 1]. feed_completeness is carried verbatim from the triggering venue because Binance forceOrder is throttled and is a cross-check, not a census. response_bps_5s and response_bps_30s are (reference_price at the horizon minus reference_price_at_burst) divided by reference_price_at_burst times ten thousand, where the horizon reading is the ready spot-reference decision with the greatest reference_time at or before burst_time plus the horizon and within 10000 milliseconds of it; an unresolved horizon publishes zero and is identified only by horizon_state, which is the authoritative field for what has resolved. expected_direction is down for longs_liquidated, up for shorts_liquidated and none for balanced. follow_through is follow_through when the sign of response_bps_30s matches expected_direction and its absolute value is at or above response_threshold_bps, fade when the sign is opposite and the absolute value is at or above the threshold, muted when the absolute value is below the threshold, and unresolved until horizon_state reaches both_resolved; response_threshold_bps defaults to 5. State is bounded to exactly one tracked cascade: a new cascade arriving before the horizons resolve replaces the tracked one, and a replaced cascade's unresolved horizons are never revised. Before the first cascade of the publisher epoch the instance is warming with reason liquidation_burst_not_observed; afterwards the identity restates the latest cascade on the interval refresh. time_since_burst_ms is a duration and therefore outside the change key, so it refreshes on the interval rather than triggering a publication (docs/CONTRACTS.md publication cadence). The Binance USD-M forceOrder stream is not carried from our hosts (rulings E30/E34/E62), so only a Bybit cascade triggers this identity; a Bybit-only cascade publishes burst_side from the E55 skew sign (a positive side_skew_60s is longs_liquidated with expected_direction down, a negative is shorts_liquidated with expected_direction up) and publishes the skew verbatim in burst_side_skew. Decimal outputs are rounded to eight places using round-half-to-even.
